column1: # tests/seat-feeder/rows.tsv — the seat rows these three instruments feed
# (U-D12, dotfiles#315). One line per row that exists on disk under the
# rewrite's meters directory.
# WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE TABLE FROM timers.tsv. A row and its timer are two
# facts, and the bug this unit fixes is exactly the case where the first exists
# without the second: the five live rows were stamped once, at 02:22, and then
# nobody wrote them again (spec section 2.4, finding C7). So the fixture seeds
# every row here at tick 0 — the rows as they stand on a box with no feeder —
# and only then lets the declared timers run. Remove a timer and its row is
# still THERE; it is merely stale, which is the refusal the mutation must show.
# columns, tab-separated:
#   row               the row id, i.e. the file stem under the meters directory
#   instrument        which of the three feeders writes it
#   owner             tom | third-party (no kernel row is fed here: the kernel
#                     re-stamps its own at every probe, spec section 2.4)
#   expected_grade    MEASURED, or UNKNOWN for a row that must refuse and say why
# cc3 is declared UNKNOWN on purpose. D-B5's MEASURED reading of 11:39Z found
# cc and cc2 answering and cc3's OAuth token expired ("TOM LINE: run `claude`
# once on cc3"), so the fixture keeps that state: a Claude seat whose reader
# refuses still gets a FRESH row every tick, carrying the refusal and its
# reason. A stale UNKNOWN and a fresh UNKNOWN are different facts, and only the
# second one tells the door why it is shut.
